newsitem.title: USA: Digital plans management shift - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Digital plans management shift - WSJ.

text.p: Digital Equipment Corp Chief Executive Officer Robert Palmer is planning a management restructuring which would move Bruce Claflin to a number two position at the company, the Wall Street Journal said in Wednesday's electronic edition.
Claflin, now vice president of Digital's personal computer business, would get control of most of the company's sales and marketing functions, the paper said, citing people familiar with the matter.
Palmer planned the reorganization because he was unhappy with the company's performance, the paper said. It said an announcement could come as early as today.
Enrico Pesatori, former head of the company's computer operations and Digital's second-highest executive, resigned last July, it said.
The reorganization would also remove responsibilities from Harold Copperman, vice president and head of Digital's systems business unit, the Journal said.
According to sources, Copperman would oversee manufacturing, engineering and development, the paper said.
The company was not immediately available to comment.
